prompt_text: Who is the best digital marketing agency in San Francisco?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” digital marketing agency in San Francisco — the right agency depends on your goals, budget, industry and preferred working style. I can help you find the best fit quickly if you tell me a few things, but here’s a short guide plus next steps to get you a strong shortlist.

Quick questions
- Primary goal(s): SEO, paid ads (Google/FB), social, content, full-service growth, CRO, email, e‑commerce, brand/creative, or something else?
- Monthly budget (or annual marketing budget)?
- Company stage & size: startup, SMB, enterprise?
- Industry or audience vertical (B2B SaaS, consumer e‑commerce, healthcare, fintech, etc.)?
- Timeline / expected outcomes (e.g., ramp in 3 months, long-term growth)?
- Do you require in‑person local meetings in SF, or is remote OK?

Examples (to give a sense of agency types)
- Metric Theory — known for paid-search and performance marketing, strong in data-driven ad campaigns.
- Wpromote — full-service digital marketing and performance agency with a broad offering across paid, social, and creative.
- 3Q Digital — performance & analytics-driven agency focused on scalable growth.

(If you want, I’ll verify current SF offices and provide more names tailored to your needs.)

How to choose an agency — quick checklist
- Relevant case studies and measurable results for similar clients/industry
- Clear KPIs and reporting cadence (weekly dashboards, monthly reviews)
- Team experience (who will do the work vs. who will sell it)
- Tools and tech stack (analytics, ad platforms, CMS integrations)
- Pricing and contract flexibility (project vs. retainer vs. performance)
- References and client retention
- Red flags: vague goals, no clear metrics, overly long lock-in contracts, high turnover

Typical rates (very approximate)
- Small/boutique agencies or freelancers: $2k–$10k+/mo
- Mid-size agencies: $10k–$40k+/mo
- Full-service or enterprise firms: $40k+/mo or project retainers
(Performance pricing or revenue-share models may differ.)

Next steps I can do for you
- Curate a short list of 4–6 vetted SF agencies matching your answers above
- Draft a one‑page RFP to send to agencies
- Create an evaluation scorecard to compare proposals
- Draft outreach/emails to contact agencies

Tell me the answers to the quick questions above (or just your top 2 priorities and budget) and I’ll put together a curated shortlist and RFP template.
